summary: Customer runs a continuous crystallisation and wants to co-locate a Raman probe and an NIR probe on the line and fuse both data streams into a single model for solute concentration and crystal form; they ask how to configure it and whether fusion is worth the effort.

facts_stated.text: Measurement is wanted at a single point in the process line.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: at the same point in the line

facts_stated.text: Two probes are proposed: a Raman probe and an NIR probe.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: combine a Raman probe and an NIR probe

facts_stated.text: Both data streams are to be fused into one model.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: fusing both data streams into one model

fluorophore.enquiry_quote: combine a Raman probe and an NIR probe

process.enquiry_quote: at the same point in the line
at the same point in the line

customer_premises.claim: A Raman probe and an NIR probe can be combined at one and the same point in the line.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: combine a Raman probe and an NIR probe at the same point in the line

customer_premises.claim: A single fused model of the two data streams is the right way to obtain both solute concentration and crystal form.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: fusing both data streams into one model for solute concentration and crystal form

customer_premises.claim: Fusing the two techniques is a worthwhile effort, to be confirmed rather than demonstrated from stated facts.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: is fusing the two worth the effort?

customer_premises.claim: A concrete setup can be prescribed now, before the deciding facts (matrix, ranges, conditions) are known.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: How should we set this up

unknowns: Which solute is to be measured and over what concentration range.
What 'crystal form' means here: which polymorphs/hydrates/particle attributes are to be distinguished and at what level.
Solvent, mother-liquor composition and other dissolved species present.
Interfering species (absorbing, scattering or fluorescent) in the stream.
Temperature and pressure at the intended measurement point.
Solids loading and crystal size distribution in the stream.
Optical behaviour at process conditions (scattering, turbidity, absorption).
Installation point in the line, interface type, optical path length and probe-to-process distance.
Fouling behaviour and cleaning regime (e.g. CIP) and window/probe maintenance.
Required accuracy, precision, detection limit and response time for solute concentration and crystal form.
Reference method used for validation and calibration.
Whether the Raman and NIR probes already exist or are to be selected; whether they can share one port.
Calibration, model transfer and maintenance strategy for a fused model.
